newsitem.title: USA: UPS obtains restraining order against pilots.
newsitem.headline: UPS obtains restraining order against pilots.

text.p: United Parcel Service said on Thursday night it won a temporary restraining order against its pilots that blocks them from intimidating pilots of independently chartered planes hired by the shipper.

The restraining order was granted late on Thursday by Jefferson County Circuit Court Judge Ellen Ewing. It effectively blocks the 2,000-member Independent Pilots Association from doing anything that might induce charter pilots not to fly UPS packages.

UPS filed suit seeking a permanent restraining order as well as unspecified damages against its pilots, who have refused to fly the company's planes in an agreement with striking Teamsters not to cross picket lines.

"The pilots are intimidating (the charter pilots), threatening to blacklist them, threatening them with the loss of (airplane) jump-seat privileges ... and other intentional acts," UPS spokesman Ken Shapero said in Louisville.
The union sought to have the case moved to federal court, but a U.S. District Court judge immediately ordered it back to state court.
Union attorney Herb Segal said the pilots' actions were protected under free speech rights.
Shapero said the restraining order applied to all its half-dozen hubs, including its main package hub in Louisville.
On Wednesday, the company chartered six large jets and 30 smaller planes to supplement the 42 company-owned planes being flown by management crews.
The other plaintiffs in the lawsuit were two charter aircraft companies, McMinnville, Ore.-based Evergreen International Aviation Inc. and Burbank, Calif.-based Ameriflight Inc.
Earlier Thursday, Independent Pilots Association President Robert Miller said the pilots could stage a strike of their own near Christmas against UPS.
